description:
FILED s543p (Opus 5.5, 2026-11-27, CODE 496df8b1 = MAIN-READY-113 caf9c693, v2-16400) by the Rosetta census (docs/rosetta-plan.md step 1; #2104).

THE SHAPE (neutral reproducer, no strict, run on the tree, perl 5.40.3 vs PCL):

    %h = (a => 1); @a = (1); $x = 1; my %mh = (b => 2);
    $r1 = \%h;  print "1 ", ref(\$r1), "\n";      # perl REF   PCL SCALAR
    $r2 = \@a;  print "2 ", ref(\$r2), "\n";      # perl REF   PCL SCALAR
    $r3 = \$x;  print "3 ", ref(\$r3), "\n";      # both REF
    $r4 = \%mh; print "4 ", ref(\$r4), "\n";      # perl REF   PCL SCALAR  (a lexical hash, a package scalar)
    $r5 = {};   print "5 ", ref(\$r5), "\n";      # both REF
    my $r6 = \%h; print "6 ", ref(\$r6), "\n";    # both REF   (a lexical scalar is right)
    $r7 = \%h;  my $rr = \$r7; print "7 ", ref($rr), " ", ref($$rr), "\n";   # perl REF HASH   PCL SCALAR HASH

So the deref is right (`ref($$rr)` is HASH); only the kind of the outer reference is wrong, and only for a PACKAGE scalar whose value is a reference to a NAMED aggregate.  Suspect: the package scalar stores the aggregate itself as its value (docs/boxed-aggregates-design-s455.md: a reference to a named array / hash is the container object), and `p-ref` of `(p-backslash $r1)` classifies the box by its value's type, where a container value is not recognised as "a reference" -- `{}` goes through a different value shape and is.  The lexical path (`my $r6`) answers REF, so the classifier has a second reading somewhere (CLAUDE.md: look for the second copy first).

CHEAP DISCRIMINATING MEASUREMENT (taken): rows 4-6 -- the named-aggregate referent with a package scalar is the only failing combination (`my` scalar right, anon referent right, scalar referent right).

THE PROGRAM: 1480-Type-detection prints `ref` of a reference to each kind of variable, written without `strict` (package variables); the "reference to a reference" line says SCALAR.
subject: SILENT WRONG: `ref(\$s)` is SCALAR where perl says REF when the PACKAGE scalar $s holds a reference to a NAMED array or hash (`$s = \%h; ref(\$s)`); a `my` scalar, an anonymous `{}` / `[]`, or `\$x` are right (Rosetta 1480)
triage_reason: ref() of a reference to a reference is core (perlfunc ref: "REF"); IN by docs/supported-subset.md section 3
